scenario: 系统设计面，面试官问「加一台机器时怎么少搬数据」。你想说一致性哈希，却说成 consistent hash，还卡在 make the keys spread even。
scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked how to move as little data as possible when adding a machine. You mean consistent hashing but say "consistent hash" and stall on "make the keys spread even."
q: 「一致性哈希，加节点只搬邻近的键」这句怎么说出口？
q_en: How do you say "consistent hashing — adding a node only moves the neighboring keys"?
options: we use the consistent hash, so the keys spread even, and when we add one the hashing is consistent, so...
so there's this ring, and the nodes sit on it, and the keys sit on it too, so if a new node joins only some keys move, only some of them, yeah...
We hash the nodes and keys onto a ring, so adding a node only reshuffles the keys next to it.
Consistent hashing maps nodes and keys onto a circular hash space to minimize key remapping under topology change.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 直译卡壳：ring 加「只挪相邻键」点名机制；consistent hash 掉了 -ing，spread even 只说结果没说为什么。
why: 术语别丢 -ing，读作一致性哈希；节点和键都放上 ring，点明加节点只挪相邻键，才证明你懂它省搬迁。
why_en: We hash the nodes and keys onto a ring, so adding a node only reshuffles the keys next to it.
whenOtherWins: 只有给非技术的人打比方时才用 ring thing、spread even；正式面试要 consistent hashing 加只挪相邻键。
options_en: we use the consistent hash, so the keys spread even, and when we add one the hashing is consistent, so...
so there's this ring, and the nodes sit on it, and the keys sit on it too, so if a new node joins only some keys move, only some of them, yeah...
We hash the nodes and keys onto a ring, so adding a node only reshuffles the keys next to it.
Consistent hashing maps nodes and keys onto a circular hash space to minimize key remapping under topology change.
optionMeanings: 掉了 -ing 说成 consistent hash，只讲 spread even。
ring、nodes 都对，但一直绕没落术语。
节点键都上 ring，点明只挪相邻键。
circular hash space 学术腔，像念论文。
optionMeanings_en: Ring and nodes right, but circles without the term.
Nodes and keys on a ring, only neighbors move.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方以为你只会背名词，不懂省搬迁。
听不出术语，像临场瞎凑。
对方立刻懂加节点为何少搬数据。
太学术，像背定义不像讲方案。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They think you only recall the name.
No term surfaces — sounds improvised.
They instantly get why little data moves.
Too academic — a definition, not a design.
optionDirectness: 错在词形：consistent hash 掉了 -ing。
错在粒度：绕圈没落到术语。
抓住 ring 加只挪相邻键的机制。
错在语域：学术词太书面。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong grain: circles, no term lands.
Nails the ring plus neighbors-only move.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把节点和键都哈希到一个环上，加减节点只影响环上相邻的一段键，搬迁最小。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing hashes nodes and keys onto a ring, so adding or removing a node only remaps the keys next to it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 首尾相接的哈希值环，节点和键按哈希值落在环上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash ring is a circular hash space where both nodes and keys are placed by their hash value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一部分键重新分配到别的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To reshuffle is to reassign some keys to a different node.

scenario: 系统设计面，面试官问「一堆节点里谁来协调」。你想说选主，却说成 leader selection，还卡在 it leads the others。
scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked who coordinates among a group of nodes. You mean leader election but say "leader selection" and stall on "it leads the others."
q: 「节点里选出一个 leader，其他 follow」这句怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "the nodes elect one leader and the rest follow"?
options: The nodes run a leader election — one gets elected leader and the rest just follow it.
we do a leader selection, so we select one node as the leader, and it leads the others, the leader is selected...
so, one of the nodes, it kind of becomes the main one, and then the others, they listen to it, and if it goes away another one takes over, yeah...
A leader election protocol designates a single coordinator node to which the remaining follower nodes defer.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs Chinglish：election 加 elect/follow 点名机制；leader selection 是词形错，the main one 太口水没术语。
why: 术语是 leader election，不是 selection，动词用 elect；一个 elected leader，其余 follow，这条链才像懂选主。
why_en: The nodes run a leader election — one gets elected leader and the rest just follow it.
whenOtherWins: 只有给非技术同事讲流程才用 the main one；正式面试要 leader election、elect、follow。
options_en: The nodes run a leader election — one gets elected leader and the rest just follow it.
we do a leader selection, so we select one node as the leader, and it leads the others, the leader is selected...
so, one of the nodes, it kind of becomes the main one, and then the others, they listen to it, and if it goes away another one takes over, yeah...
A leader election protocol designates a single coordinator node to which the remaining follower nodes defer.
optionMeanings: election 加 elect/follow，选主链紧凑。
把 election 说成 selection，词形错。
全程 the main one，绕圈没术语。
designates/defer 公文腔，像念协议。
optionMeanings_en: Election plus elect/follow — a tight chain.
All "the main one," circles, no term.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方懂你选主、其余跟随。
词形错，像没真做过选主。
听不出机制，像临场瞎凑。
太书面，像背协议不像讲系统。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They get you elect one, rest follow.
Wrong form — doubts you've done it.
No mechanism — sounds improvised.
Too written — a protocol, not your system.
optionDirectness: 抓住 election 加 elect、follow 机制。
错在词形：selection 不是 election。
错在粒度：绕圈没点选主术语。
错在语域：公文体太僵。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong grain: circles, no election term.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组节点通过约定选出一个 leader 来协调，其余成为 follower。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Leader election is how a group of nodes picks one leader to coordinate while the rest become followers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 动词，选出某个节点当 leader。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To elect is to choose one node to be the leader.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跟随 leader、接受它决定的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A follower is a node that defers to the leader's decisions.

scenario: 系统设计面，聊到网络分区。面试官问「两边都自认为 leader 会怎样」，你想说脑裂，却说成 brain split，还绕在 both are the boss。
scenario_en: In a system design round on network partitions, the interviewer asks what happens when both sides think they're leader. You mean split-brain but say "brain split" and circle on "both are the boss."
q: 「分区后两个节点都自认为 leader」这个词怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "after a partition two nodes both think they're the leader"?
options: we get a brain split, so the two nodes, they both are the leader now, the brain is split into two sides...
so when the network breaks, one side can't see the other, and then both of them start acting like the boss, both of them, and that's bad, yeah...
A network partition may induce a split-brain condition wherein two nodes concurrently assume leadership.
After a partition you can hit split-brain — two nodes both think they're leader and both take writes.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 词序倒装：split-brain 加「都收写」点名危害；brain split 倒了词序，the boss 太口水没术语。
why: 术语是 split-brain，连字符，别倒成 brain split；点明两节点都自认 leader、都收写，才说清危害。
why_en: After a partition you can hit split-brain — two nodes both think they're leader and both take writes.
whenOtherWins: 只有轻松打比方时才说 both act like the boss；正式面试要 split-brain 加两边都收写。
options_en: we get a brain split, so the two nodes, they both are the leader now, the brain is split into two sides...
so when the network breaks, one side can't see the other, and then both of them start acting like the boss, both of them, and that's bad, yeah...
A network partition may induce a split-brain condition wherein two nodes concurrently assume leadership.
After a partition you can hit split-brain — two nodes both think they're leader and both take writes.
optionMeanings: 词序倒成 brain split，还说 the boss。
network breaks 对，但绕圈没落术语。
induce/concurrently 学术腔，像念论文。
split-brain 加两边都收写，危害到位。
optionMeanings_en: "Network breaks" right, but circles, no term.
Split-brain plus both take writes — risk lands.
optionScenarioImpacts: 词序倒了，像没真踩过脑裂。
听不出术语，像临场瞎凑。
太学术，像背定义不像讲故障。
对方懂脑裂危害是双写冲突。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Reversed form — doubts you've hit it.
No term — sounds improvised.
Too academic — a definition, not a failure.
They get split-brain means conflicting writes.
optionDirectness: 错在词序：brain split 倒装。
错在粒度：绕圈没点 split-brain。
错在语域：学术词太书面。
抓住 split-brain 加双写危害。
optionDirectness_en: Nails split-brain plus the double-write risk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络分区后两个节点各自以为自己是 leader，都对外接受写，导致数据冲突。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Split-brain is when a partition leaves two nodes each believing it's the leader, both taking writes and conflicting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集群被网络故障切成互相看不见的两半。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A network partition is when a network fault splits the cluster into halves that can't see each other.

scenario: 系统设计面，问「谁存 leader 租约和配置」。你想说用 ZooKeeper 这类协调服务，却说成 a manage service，还卡在 it keeps the config。
scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked who stores the leader lease and config. You mean a coordination service like ZooKeeper but say "a manage service" and stall on "it keeps the config."
q: 「用 ZooKeeper 这类协调服务管租约、配置、成员」怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "use a coordination service like ZooKeeper for the lease, config, and membership"?
options: we use a manage service like the ZooKeeper, so it keeps the config and knows who is alive, the service manages...
We use a coordination service like ZooKeeper to hold the leader lease, config, and membership.
so there's this thing, like ZooKeeper, and it kind of stores stuff, the config and who's the leader, and who's around, all of that, yeah...
A coordination service such as ZooKeeper maintains the leader lease, configuration state, and cluster membership.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs Chinglish：coordination service 加 lease/config/membership 点全职责；manage service 是造词，keeps stuff 太模糊。
why: 说的是协调服务 like ZooKeeper，别自己造词；一口气点 lease、config、membership 三件事，才像用过。
why_en: We use a coordination service like ZooKeeper to hold the leader lease, config, and membership.
whenOtherWins: 只有对方不熟 ZooKeeper 要你先解释时才说 it stores stuff；随后仍要落回 lease、config、membership。
options_en: we use a manage service like the ZooKeeper, so it keeps the config and knows who is alive, the service manages...
We use a coordination service like ZooKeeper to hold the leader lease, config, and membership.
so there's this thing, like ZooKeeper, and it kind of stores stuff, the config and who's the leader, and who's around, all of that, yeah...
A coordination service such as ZooKeeper maintains the leader lease, configuration state, and cluster membership.
optionMeanings: 造词 manage service，还多个 the。
coordination service 加租约配置成员，全。
this thing、stores stuff，绕圈没术语。
maintains/configuration state 公文腔。
optionMeanings_en: "This thing, stores stuff" — circles, no term.
optionScenarioImpacts: 造词露怯，像没真用过协调服务。
对方懂你拿它管租约、配置、成员。
听不出职责，像临场瞎凑。
太书面，像背文档不像讲选型。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Coined term — doubts you've used it.
They see you use it for lease/config/members.
No responsibilities — sounds improvised.
Too written — a doc, not a choice.
optionDirectness: 错在词形：manage service 是造词。
抓住协调服务加三项职责。
错在粒度：stores stuff 太泛。
错在语域：公文体太僵。
optionDirectness_en: Nails the service plus its three jobs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 像 ZooKeeper 这样的组件，替集群统一存租约、配置、成员这些一致性状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A coordination service like ZooKeeper is a component that holds cluster-wide state such as leases, config, and membership.

termDefinitions.meaning: leader 持有的一段有时限的授权，到期不续就失去 leader 身份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A leader lease is a time-bounded grant a leader holds; if it isn't renewed it loses leadership.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集群当前有哪些活着的节点这份名单。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Membership is the current list of live nodes in the cluster.

scenario: 系统设计面，问「跨服务的下单事务怎么保证」。你想说用 saga 而不是两阶段提交，却说成 two phase submit，还卡在 roll back everything。
scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked how to keep an order transaction consistent across services. You mean a saga over two-phase commit but say "two phase submit" and stall on "roll back everything."
q: 「跨服务不用 2PC，用 saga 加补偿」这句怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "across services, skip 2PC and use a saga with compensation"?
options: we do a two phase submit, or we can do a saga, so it commits in two phase and then submit, the phases...
so instead of doing the big lock thing across all of them, we let each one do its own part, and if one fails we undo the earlier ones, undo them one by one, yeah...
Across services I'd use a saga over two-phase commit — each step commits locally, with a compensating action to undo on failure.
Rather than a two-phase commit, a saga executes local transactions with compensating transactions to preserve consistency.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs Chinglish：saga 加 compensating action 点名机制；two phase submit 是词形错，the big lock thing 太口水。
why: 术语是 two-phase commit，别说 submit；saga 是各步 local commit 加 compensating action，失败就补偿，这句才像懂。
why_en: Across services I'd use a saga over two-phase commit — each step commits locally, with a compensating action to undo on failure.
whenOtherWins: 只有对方要强一致、能接受阻塞时才提 2PC；默认跨服务用 saga 加补偿。
options_en: we do a two phase submit, or we can do a saga, so it commits in two phase and then submit, the phases...
so instead of doing the big lock thing across all of them, we let each one do its own part, and if one fails we undo the earlier ones, undo them one by one, yeah...
Across services I'd use a saga over two-phase commit — each step commits locally, with a compensating action to undo on failure.
Rather than a two-phase commit, a saga executes local transactions with compensating transactions to preserve consistency.
optionMeanings: 把 commit 说成 submit，还混着说。
the big lock thing 大白话，绕圈没术语。
saga 对比 2PC，补偿动作点到位。
executes/preserve 公文腔，像念论文。
optionMeanings_en: "The big lock thing" plain talk, no term.
Saga vs 2PC, names the compensating action.
optionScenarioImpacts: 词形错，像没真做过分布式事务。
听不出术语，像临场瞎凑。
对方懂你用 saga、失败靠补偿。
太书面，像背定义不像讲选型。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Wrong form — doubts you've done distributed tx.
No term — sounds improvised.
They get saga plus compensating on failure.
Too written — a definition, not a choice.
optionDirectness: 错在词形：submit 不是 commit。
错在粒度：大白话没点 saga、补偿。
抓住 saga 对比 2PC 加补偿。
错在语域：学术词太书面。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong grain: plain talk, no saga/compensation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 简称 2PC；协调者先让所有参与者 prepare，都同意才一起 commit，有一个不行就全回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-phase commit (2PC) has a coordinator ask all participants to prepare, then commit only if everyone agrees, else roll back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个大事务拆成若干本地事务，某步失败就对已完成的步骤逐个执行补偿动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A saga splits one transaction into local steps; if a step fails, it runs a compensating action to undo each completed step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 撤销某个已提交本地步骤的反向操作，比如已扣款就退款。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A compensating action is a reverse operation that undoes a committed local step, e.g. a refund for a charge.

scenario: 系统设计面，问「网络分区时你保一致还是保可用」。你想说 CAP 里二选一，却说成 CAP theory、choose two of three，没落到 CP/AP。
scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked, during a partition, whether you keep consistency or availability. You mean the CAP choice but say "CAP theory" and "choose two of three," never landing on CP/AP.
q: 「分区时 CAP 逼你在一致和可用里二选一」怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "under a partition CAP forces a choice between consistency and availability"?
options: Under a partition CAP forces a choice — go CP and reject writes, or go AP and serve maybe-stale data.
by the CAP theory we choose two of the three, so we pick the C and the A, or the P, two of three...
so when the network splits, you can't have both, you have to give up one, either the consistent one or the up one, you pick one, yeah...
The CAP theorem stipulates that under a partition a system must forfeit either consistency or availability.
tradeoff: 地道落点 vs 口号复述：CP/AP 加各自代价点名取舍；choose two of three 是常见误读，没落到分区下的真选择。
why: CAP 只在 partition 下二选一，不是「三选二」；要落到 CP 拒写保一致、AP 可用但可能读到旧值。
why_en: Under a partition CAP forces a choice — go CP and reject writes, or go AP and serve maybe-stale data.
whenOtherWins: 只有科普 CAP 由来时才提三个字母；正式答要落到分区下 CP 还是 AP。
options_en: Under a partition CAP forces a choice — go CP and reject writes, or go AP and serve maybe-stale data.
by the CAP theory we choose two of the three, so we pick the C and the A, or the P, two of three...
so when the network splits, you can't have both, you have to give up one, either the consistent one or the up one, you pick one, yeah...
The CAP theorem stipulates that under a partition a system must forfeit either consistency or availability.
optionMeanings: 落到 CP 拒写、AP 旧读，取舍到位。
复述 two of three，没落到分区选择。
the up one 大白话，绕圈没术语。
stipulates/forfeit 公文腔，像念定理。
optionMeanings_en: Lands on CP-reject vs AP-stale — the tradeoff.
Recites "two of three," no partition choice.
"The up one" plain talk, circles, no term.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方懂分区下你会怎么取舍。
停在口号，像只背过定理。
听不出 CP/AP，像临场瞎凑。
太书面，像背定理不像做决定。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They see how you'd trade off in a partition.
Stuck on the slogan — only memorized it.
No CP/AP — sounds improvised.
Too written — a theorem, not a decision.
optionDirectness: 抓住分区下 CP／AP 各自代价。
错在误读：三选二不是 CAP 重点。
错在粒度：大白话没点 CP／AP。
错在语域：定理腔太书面。
optionDirectness_en: Nails CP/AP costs under a partition.
Wrong read: "two of three" misses the point.
Wrong grain: plain talk, no CP/AP.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式系统在网络分区时，只能在强一致和高可用里选一个保住。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP says that during a network partition a distributed system can keep either strong consistency or high availability, not both.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区时选一致：宁可拒绝请求也不返回不一致的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CP means choosing consistency in a partition: reject requests rather than return inconsistent data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区时选可用：继续响应，但可能返回旧数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AP means choosing availability in a partition: keep responding, but the data may be stale.

scenario: 系统设计面，问「怎么知道一个节点还活着」。你想说靠心跳和租约，却说成 send heart beat、alive signal，还卡在 kick it out。
scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked how you know a node is still alive. You mean heartbeats and a lease but say "send heart beat" and "alive signal," and stall on "kick it out."
q: 「节点靠心跳续租约，漏跳就被剔除」这句怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "a node holds its lease via heartbeats; miss them and it's evicted"?
options: each node sends a heart beat, like an alive signal, and if no signal we kick it out, the beat shows it's alive...
so every node keeps sending a little ping, like i'm here, i'm here, and if it stops for a while then we take it out of the group, yeah...
Each node periodically emits a heartbeat to renew its lease; upon expiry the node is deemed failed and removed.
Each node sends a heartbeat to hold its lease — miss a few and the cluster marks it dead and evicts it.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 拆词口水：heartbeat 加 lease、evict 点名机制；heart beat 拆开了，alive signal、kick out 太口水。
why: 术语是 heartbeat，一个词，别拆成 heart beat，再加 lease；点明漏跳到租约过期到被 evict，才说清存活检测。
why_en: Each node sends a heartbeat to hold its lease — miss a few and the cluster marks it dead and evicts it.
whenOtherWins: 只有对非技术的人打比方才说 keeps pinging i'm here；正式面试要 heartbeat、lease、evict。
options_en: each node sends a heart beat, like an alive signal, and if no signal we kick it out, the beat shows it's alive...
so every node keeps sending a little ping, like i'm here, i'm here, and if it stops for a while then we take it out of the group, yeah...
Each node periodically emits a heartbeat to renew its lease; upon expiry the node is deemed failed and removed.
Each node sends a heartbeat to hold its lease — miss a few and the cluster marks it dead and evicts it.
optionMeanings: heart beat 拆成两词，还说 kick out。
keeps pinging 大白话，绕圈没术语。
emits/deemed 公文腔，像念规范。
heartbeat 续租约、漏跳被剔，机制全。
optionScenarioImpacts: 拆词露怯，像没真做过存活检测。
听不出术语，像临场瞎凑。
太书面，像背规范不像讲机制。
对方懂心跳续租、漏跳即剔除。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Split term — doubts you've done liveness.
No term — sounds improvised.
Too written — a spec, not a mechanism.
They get heartbeat-renews, miss-then-evict.
optionDirectness: 错在词形：heart beat 拆成两词。
错在粒度：大白话没点 lease、evict。
错在语域：规范腔太书面。
抓住心跳续租加漏跳剔除。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong form: "heart beat" split in two.
Wrong grain: plain talk, no lease/evict.

termDefinitions.meaning: 节点周期性发出的存活信号，用来证明自己还活着。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a periodic liveness signal a node sends to prove it's still alive.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一段有时限的存活授权，靠心跳续期，过期就被判失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lease is a time-bounded liveness grant renewed by heartbeats; when it expires the node is treated as failed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把失联的节点从集群成员里剔除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To evict is to remove an unresponsive node from the cluster's membership.

scenario: 系统设计面，问「一个节点特别热怎么办」。你想说做 rebalancing 把分片挪走，却说成 re-balance the load、move the data around。
scenario_en: In a system design round you're asked what to do when one node runs hot. You mean rebalancing to move partitions off it but say "re-balance the load" and "move the data around."
q: 「节点热了就 rebalance，把部分分片挪走匀负载」怎么说？
q_en: How do you say "when a node runs hot, rebalance by moving some partitions off it"?
options: we re-balance the load, so we move the data around to make it even, the load gets balanced, move it around...
When a node runs hot we rebalance — move some of its partitions elsewhere to even out the load.
so this one machine has too much on it, so we take some of its stuff and put it on the others, spread it out a bit, yeah...
When a node becomes hot, partitions are redistributed across the cluster to equalize load and preserve data locality.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 泛泛匀活：rebalance 加挪 partition 点名机制；re-balance the load、move data around 只说结果没说挪什么。
why: 术语是 rebalance，一个词；点明把部分 partition 挪到别处匀负载，同时尽量保住 data locality，才像调过。
why_en: When a node runs hot we rebalance — move some partitions off it to even out the load without wrecking data locality.
whenOtherWins: 只有给非技术的人讲才说 spread it out；正式面试要 rebalance 加挪 partition、data locality。
options_en: we re-balance the load, so we move the data around to make it even, the load gets balanced, move it around...
When a node runs hot we rebalance — move some of its partitions elsewhere to even out the load.
so this one machine has too much on it, so we take some of its stuff and put it on the others, spread it out a bit, yeah...
When a node becomes hot, partitions are redistributed across the cluster to equalize load and preserve data locality.
optionMeanings: 说成 re-balance the load，只讲匀活。
rebalance 加挪 partition，机制到位。
take its stuff 大白话，绕圈没术语。
redistributed/equalize 公文腔，像念文档。
optionMeanings_en: Rebalance plus moving partitions — the mechanism.
"Take its stuff" plain talk, circles, no term.
optionScenarioImpacts: 没说挪什么，像没真调过负载。
对方懂你挪 partition 来匀热点。
听不出挪的是分片，像瞎凑。
太书面，像背文档不像讲操作。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: Names nothing moved — doubts you've done it.
They get you move partitions off the hot node.
Can't tell partitions move — sounds improvised.
Too written — a doc, not an operation.
optionDirectness: 错在词形：re-balance the load 太泛。
抓住 rebalance 加挪 partition。
错在粒度：大白话没点 partition。
错在语域：公文体太僵。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong form: "re-balance the load" too vague.
Wrong grain: plain talk, no partition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 当负载或数据在节点间不均时，把一部分分片迁移到别处，让各节点趋于均衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To rebalance is to move some partitions between nodes so load evens out when it's skewed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据被切成的一片，可以整片在节点间迁移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is one slice of the data that can be moved between nodes as a unit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让计算尽量在数据所在的节点上进行，迁移分片时要权衡它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data locality means keeping computation on the node where its data lives; moving partitions trades against it.
